# Altair Code for Seattle Weather Dataset

Here are several visualization examples using the built-in `seattle-weather` dataset in Altair:

## 1. Basic Setup

```python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

# Load the dataset
source = data.seattle_weather()
```

## 2. Temperature Over Time (Line Chart)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_line().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    color=alt.value('red')
).properties(
    title='Maximum Temperature Over Time',
    width=600,
    height=300
)
```

## 3. Weather Type Distribution (Bar Chart)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_bar().encode(
    x='weather:N',
    y='count()',
    color='weather:N'
).properties(
    title='Weather Type Distribution',
    width=400,
    height=300
)
```

## 4. Temperature Range with Precipitation (Layered Chart)

```python
base = alt.Chart(source).encode(
    x='date:T'
)

temp_line = base.mark_line().encode(
    y='temp_max:Q',
    color=alt.value('red')
)

temp_band = base.mark_area(opacity=0.3).encode(
    y='temp_min:Q',
    y2='temp_max:Q'
)

precipitation = base.mark_bar().encode(
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color=alt.value('steelblue')
)

(temp_line + temp_band + precipitation).properties(
    title='Temperature Range and Precipitation',
    width=700,
    height=400
)
```

## 5. Interactive Scatter Plot

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_circle(size=60).encode(
    x='temp_max:Q',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:Q', 'temp_min:Q', 'precipitation:Q', 'weather:N']
).interactive().properties(
    title='Temperature vs Precipitation',
    width=500,
    height=400
)
```

## 6. Monthly Average Temperature (Aggregated)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(temp_max):Q',
    color=alt.value('orange')
).properties(
    title='Average Monthly Maximum Temperature',
    width=500,
    height=300
)
```

## Installation

If you haven't installed the required packages:

```bash
pip install altair vega_datasets
```

## Display in Jupyter Notebook

```python
# Enable the renderer
alt.renderers.enable('default')

# Display any chart
chart  # Just reference the chart variable
```

## Key Encoding Types

- `:T` - Temporal (dates)
- `:Q` - Quantitative (numbers)
- `:N` - Nominal (categories)
- `:O` - Ordinal (ordered categories)

These examples cover the most common visualization patterns for this dataset. You can customize colors, sizes, titles, and add interactivity based on your needs! 😊
